transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hi berry :) ok so it was in my grandma's kitchen, the one from when i was little. there was this old phone on the wall ringing and nobody answered it. and she just kept cutting a cake, slice after slice, but it never got any smaller. that's the bit that's stuck with me

a cake that never gets any smaller, with the phone just ringing and ringing. that's such a strange pair

where were you while she was cutting it?

just in the kitchen with her i think, i don't really remember where exactly. my uncle ray was there too, leaning in the doorway smoking. and then the walls started moving in, slowly, like the kitchen was shrinking around us

oh, the walls moving in, slowly. while she's still cutting and ray's just leaning there

did anyone else seem to notice the kitchen shrinking?

i don't remember anyone reacting to it honestly. grandma just kept cutting. and then i looked down and i was a kid again, in this red cardigan i used to wear. which was weird because the whole dream was black and white, like an old film with scratches on it, but the cardigan was red

everything grey and scratchy, and then just that red cardigan

what was it like, looking down and finding yourself little again?
honestly i don't really remember how it felt, it just kind of was that way, the way dreams are. and the phone was still ringing when i woke up, that's what i remember most

that's fine, dreams are like that. and the phone still ringing as you woke, that's the kind of thing that follows you out

if you could stop the dream on one moment and just hold it there, which would it be? and what's in front of you right then?

probably when i looked down and i was little in the red cardigan. grandma at the table still cutting the cake, ray in the doorway, the phone ringing on the wall, and the walls coming in. oh and there was a big round clock and a checked floor, i forgot those before. everything grey except the cardigan

a big round clock and a checked floor, all grey, and you in that red cardigan in the middle of it

the clock, do you remember anything about it?
not really, just that it was big and round. i don't remember what time it said or anything

that's fine, big and round is enough

with all that stuff in the kitchen, the phone, the cake, the clock, was there anything that felt like it really mattered? or nothing in particular?

probably the phone, just cause it never stopped ringing and nobody picked it up. and it was still going when i woke up. the cake too i guess, it was so weird that it never got smaller. but i don't know if they meant anything

ok so you're in your grandma's kitchen, the one from when you were little. it's all black and white with scratches on it, like something really old, with a big round clock and a checked floor. she's at the table cutting a cake, slice after slice, and it never gets any smaller. your uncle ray is leaning in the doorway smoking, and an old phone on the wall keeps ringing and nobody answers it. then the walls start moving in, slowly, and nobody reacts, grandma just keeps cutting. you look down and you're a kid again in your red cardigan, the only thing that isn't grey. and the phone is still ringing when you wake up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it pretty much. only thing, the phone was the old kind with a long curly cord. and it was like an old film, with scratches on it. otherwise yeah that's the dream

the long curly cord, yes, i can see it hanging down the wall

so it's your grandma's kitchen, all black and white and scratched like something really old, with the big round clock and the checked floor. she's cutting a cake that never gets smaller, ray's smoking in the doorway, and the old phone with its curly cord just keeps ringing. the walls creep in, nobody reacts, and you look down and you're little again in your red cardigan, the only bit of colour. and the phone's still ringing when you wake

is that how it went, or is there anything you'd change?
yeah that's how it went. only thing, it was like an old film specifically, with the scratches. but otherwise that's it

like an old film, scratches and all. got it

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah i'd love that actually

ok, a few ways it could look. smudgy grey charcoal, soft like a worn memory, with just the cardigan in red. or like an old family photo found in a drawer, silvery grey, with someone's carefully painted the cardigan red. or crisp black ink like an old storybook, where the kitchen doesn't quite sit still, with one red bit. or just how you saw it, a scratchy old black and white film with you in bright red in the middle

which feels closest, or would you describe it your own way?
the last one, like the old scratchy film with me in red. that's how it looked

the old scratchy film it is. i'll start with your grandma

i'm picturing her as you knew her when you were little, an older woman in a plain house dress with an apron over it. those bits are my guesses though, you didn't say

anything different about how she looked, or leave that to me?
i don't really remember what she was wearing, so go with your guess. that sounds fine

ok, i'm sketching your grandma, her kitchen, the phone and the cake now, they'll show up on the right

and ray, i'm picturing him as your uncle, a middle-aged man in a casual shirt and trousers. how he looks and what he's wearing are just my guesses though

anything different about him, or leave it to me?
go with your guess, i don't remember what he had on. just that he was leaning in the doorway smoking

ok, sketching ray now, leaning in the doorway with his cigarette

everything's being drawn and it'll show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks off once it's there, just tell me
oh wow, yeah they look right. that's pretty much how i remember it

oh good, i'm glad they feel like them

the rest of it's still coming together on the right, so just tell me if anything looks off once it's all there
ok will do, so far it all looks right to me

good, so grandma, ray, the kitchen, the phone and the cake are all there now

next i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the one before, and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, the first one looks right so far. i'll wait for the rest

good, the phone ringing on the wall with nobody picking up. glad that one feels right

i'll carry on from there, the other five are on their way
ok sounds good, i'll keep an eye out for the rest
sounds good, they'll pop up on the right as they're ready
the second one's up now, looks right to me too. waiting on the rest

good, grandma cutting another slice and the cake still whole

the other four carry on from that one, so i'll draw them now and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok great, yeah the cake one looks right. i'll wait for the others
glad the cake one feels right. the other four are still on their way, they'll show up on the right soon
the third one's up now too, looks right to me. waiting on the other three

ray in the doorway with his cigarette, good, glad that one's right too

the last three carry on from him, so i'll draw those now and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, ray looks right. i'll wait for the last three

good, glad ray feels right

the last three are still coming, they'll show up on the right soon
the fourth one's up now, looks right to me. two more to go

the walls creeping in around grandma while she keeps cutting, glad that one's right

the last two carry on from there, so i'll draw them now and they'll show up on the right soon
yeah the walls one looks right. ok i'll wait for the last two

good, glad the walls one feels right

the last two are still coming, they'll show up on the right soon
the fifth one's up now, looks right. just one left

you little again in the red cardigan, the one you'd stop the dream on. glad it looks right

the last one carries on from there, so i'll draw it now and it'll show up on the right soon
yeah the cardigan one looks right, that's the moment. ok i'll wait for the last one

glad that one's the moment for you

the last one's still coming, it'll show up on the right soon
the last one's up now, looks right. that's all of it, it really does look like the dream. thanks berry

i'm really glad. your grandma's kitchen, all scratchy and grey, and you little in that red cardigan right in the middle of it

now that phone can keep ringing somewhere you can look at it whenever you like
